transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Gomez (Redwood SE), Arjun Iyer (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (AtlasPay VP Eng), Marcus Chen (AtlasPay SRE), Priya Rao (AtlasPay CTO), Ethan Park (AtlasPay Payments Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync to triage last week's partial outage impacting payments enrichment path. We reviewed root cause hypotheses, validated that large variable-length input sequences (escaped JSON payloads + repeated prompts) caused KV cache growth and GPU memory pressure which, combined with autoscaler floor settings and a metrics delay, led to OOM evictions and degraded fallback routing. Action items and canary plan agreed.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and telemetry gaps
- Autoscaler behavior and min-replica floor
- Fallback to compact model and pricing impact
- Observability and alerting improvements
- Security/POC of canary flow

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan (AE): all right everyone thanks for carving time, we'll keep tightly focused. start by quick recap. we have about 50 minutes.
00:18 Lena (VP Eng): hey thanks, yeah we want to make sure we have a clear mitigation and customer facing timeline — last friday's window hit peak txn flow and some payments were delayed.
00:28 Marcus (SRE): I can show logs later, quick note: we saw upward drift in tokenized sequence length for a subset of requests — something about the enrichment payloads. looked like repeated metadata got concatenated server-side.
00:42 Samira (SE): right, our initial trace shows the KV cache size per session ballooned ~7x for those sessions, which increased per-token memory leading to a couple of GPU OOMs. the runtime evicted and then your autoscaler didn't add replicas fast enough because min replicas were pinned low.
01:05 Priya (CTO): pinned low by what? i thought we had a committed dedicated pool for that tenant.
01:12 Jordan: you do, but there is a min-replica floor in the autoscaler config and an additional safety throttle in the control plane that prevents rapid spin-up when we've had transient metric noise — that throttle came into play.
01:26 Marcus: also our kube metrics had a 40s scrape gap during that window, so the scaler decision lagged.
01:34 Ethan (Payments Eng): to be frank, part of the problem was input shaping on our side — a retry path was appending context on failure and the resulting string blew out seq length.
01:46 Lena: there was definitely cross-team miscoordination, ok. can we walk through the proposed immediate mitigations?
01:53 Samira: short term we recommend: (1) apply an autoscaler hotfix to raise min replicas to 4 for high-traffic routes, (2) add a fast-path emergency fallback that routes a small percentage of traffic to the compact model if per-request token estimate > X, (3) tighten scrape interval for your metrics to 15s during the pilot window.
02:18 Jordan: i'll also propose a temporary credit for impacted token overage while we run the canary — won't be final, but helps close the gap.
02:28 Marcus: the fallback to compact model, what about quality? does it affect payment scoring?
02:34 Samira: good question. compact model reduces contextual window and some heuristics degrade slightly — but for enrichment we validated in earlier evals that precision drop is <2% on our test set. it's safer than an OOM.
02:50 Priya: ok acceptable for short-term. next, triggers: how do we detect the ballooning before OOM?
02:56 Samira: instrument per-request token estimator in the control plane, alert at 2.5x median, and have real-time TVM on KV growth. also add a synthetic test that sends a malformed append vector every 5 minutes to ensure fallback path works.
03:18 Marcus: action item: i'll attach the gc and dmesg dumps from the window to the ticket.
03:24 Ethan: i'll recreate the client-side bug that caused the append and share the minimal repro — should help with thresholding.
03:32 Jordan: excellent. let's walk through timeline — Samira can you outline steps to push hotfix?
03:37 Samira: yes: 1) small code patch to remove scaler throttle for pinned customers (QA 24h), 2) bump min replicas to 4 in infra config, 3) deploy fallback routing rule by feature flag. we can do sequence in 36 hours if nothing blocks.
03:55 Lena: is that work in the Dedicated plane or do you need our infra folks to approve?
04:02 Samira: it's on Redwood's control plane side, no customer infra change except metrics scrape interval. but we will need your SRE to validate log access for the canary.
04:15 Priya: security question: fallback model would be a different binary, do we need new attestation or re-approval from our infosec?
04:23 Jordan: no new secrets, same committed environment. however we'll share the model hash and audit trail. Arjun will send the artifact and the attestation link.
04:33 Arjun (CSM): noted, i'll include the model hash and a short security note.
04:38 Marcus: what about rate of rollback if fallback causes quality issues?
04:42 Samira: we'll have a 10-minute automatic rollback if certain signal thresholds (error rate, mismatch score) breach. also canary traffic will start at 1% then 5% then 20%.
04:58 Ethan: ok that sounds safe.
05:03 Lena: curious about observability gaps you mentioned earlier — we want to avoid blind spots.
05:09 Samira: main gaps: 1) tokenized sequence length wasn't surfaced in your dashboards, 2) KV cache growth not correlated with user_id/session_id in logs, 3) autoscaler decision path not emitting reasons. we'll add three small dashboards within 48h.
05:28 Marcus: re: tokenized length, we can capture that in our ingress side too, low cost.
05:33 Jordan: great. i also want to call out a couple of downstream tradeoffs: increasing min replicas will cost more short term; fallback to compact model will slightly increase per-request latency for some flows. we'll include those numbers in the pricing note.
05:52 Priya: fine if that buys reliability. we need a firm canary schedule.
05:58 Arjun: propose week of 2026-10-26 for canary on staging, small window first on staging then production on 10/28 if green.
06:06 Lena: works for us.
06:09 Jordan: ok let's put a public-facing mitigation timeline for impacted customers and a postmortem draft; who owns comms?
06:15 Lena: i'll coordinate comms with our ops comms lead once we have the canary outcome. Marcus will provide the technical appendix.
06:22 Samira: we can draft the postmortem skeleton and attach telemetry. Jordan will draft the customer credit proposal.
06:29 Marcus: question — any long-term fix? we don't want to rely on manual min replica increases forever.
06:34 Samira: long-term: smarter routing by request-shape classification, better KV eviction heuristics in runtime, and improved autoscaler that uses token-estimates rather than CPU-only signals. that's a 3-4 sprint effort.
06:51 Ethan: can we get a temporary rule that rejects requests with obviously malformed appended contexts rather than fallback?
06:58 Samira: yes, a validation filter could block or normalise those inputs at the edge. we'll add that to the follow-up backlog.
07:06 Jordan: let's capture next steps again. Samira pushes hotfix, Marcus uploads logs, Ethan sends repro, Arjun prepares canary checklist, Jordan prepares credit estimate. deadlines noted.
07:23 Lena: thanks team. any other risks?
07:28 Priya: compliance ask — will any of this change our audit trail? need to ensure fallback routing still logs full provenance.
07:35 Jordan: yes we will ensure full tracing and produce an audit artifact. Arjun will include audit trace example.
07:45 Marcus: small operational note — we should add a SLO that measures requests served without fallback over a sliding window, so we can monitor regressions.
07:54 Samira: agreed. we'll add SLO and alert playbook.
08:00 Jordan: great, we've got consensus. we'll reconvene after hotfix and one canary run. thanks all.

(occasional crosstalk, filler words, and brief pauses throughout — transcription may have swapped some proper nouns and acronyms)
